_comment: NOTE: ./load strips this _comment key with jq before POSTing, because
RavenDB rejects unknown properties on the request body.
Two static indexes over the Logs collection. PUT to
/databases/<db>/admin/indexes by ./load, after config/analyzer.cs is
installed via /admin/analyzers.
WHY TWO ENGINES
Corax cannot do fuzzy or proximity search -- CoraxQueryBuilder.cs throws
NotSupportedInCoraxException for both. That is 7 queries: Q13 (proximity)
and Q22/Q23/Q24/Q48/Q49/Q59 (fuzzy). Everything else the workload needs
(Search, Regex, StartsWith, EndsWith, Boost, Exact) Corax handles, and it
handles the distinct-count joins far better than Lucene, which materializes
the whole match set in a GatherAllCollector before deduping. So:
Logs/Search  Corax   85 queries, including all nine joins
Logs/Fuzzy   Lucene   the 7 fuzzy/proximity queries, 4 fields, nothing else
Together: 92/92. Routing queries across two indexes inside one adapter is
the established pattern here -- tiger picks between BM25, GIN and ~* per
query; elastic ships a second trace_lookup index. The convention is to
declare the mapping in the header and charge every auxiliary structure to
load_time and data_size, which ./data-size does by summing the whole
database.
SearchEngineType IS A Configuration KEY, NOT A TOP-LEVEL FIELD.
IndexDefinition has no SearchEngineType property; the key is
Indexing.Static.SearchEngineType (Constants.cs:378), scoped
ServerWideOrPerDatabaseOrPerIndex. It is set EXPLICITLY on both indexes
because the default follows the LICENSE, not the version: None/Community/
Developer get Corax, Professional/Enterprise get Lucene. Developing on a dev
license and publishing from an enterprise one would flip both engines
silently -- and the joins are where the two diverge most.
COMPUTED FIELDS
RQL 'group by' builds an AUTO MAP-REDUCE index and is unavailable over a
static index; the static-index equivalent is select facet(<field>), which
counts unique terms under an arbitrary where. Hence:
TimestampMinute  minute bucket for the histograms Q61-Q65, which other
engines derive at query time (date_trunc/date_histogram).
SeverityScope    SeverityText|ScopeName, because two facets return two
INDEPENDENT lists, not the key PAIRS Q67 asks for.
Both are per-document derived values, not pre-computed aggregates -- the
counting still happens at query time over whatever the filter matched.
TRACE FLAGS
HasPayment/HasFrontend/HasCart come from traces/<TraceId> documents via
LoadDocument, the same move elastic/build_lookup.py makes with its
trace_lookup dimension index. Those documents MUST be written before the
logs: LoadDocument registers a reference, so writing a trace document after
its logs re-indexes every log referencing it.
TraceId is stored (Storage: Yes) so the distinct-count projection is served
from the index entry rather than loading one document per matching log.
The a.TraceId != '' guard needs no expression: a log with an empty TraceId
has no traces/ document, so all three flags are false and it can never
satisfy the b-side.
REJECTED: a trace-grain term index (map fanned out one entry per token,
grouped by (TraceId, ServiceName, Term)). It works for some of the nine and
the filter would legally sit on the group-by key, but at 1B logs it yields
~10B reduce entries -- an index larger than the corpus, charged to data_size
and load_time for all 92 queries -- and it still cannot express Q86 (phrase),
Q88 or Q90, because any reduction to trace grain loses same-log token
co-occurrence. Restricting the vocabulary to the benchmark's terms to shrink
it would be precomputing the answers.

Indexes.Name: Logs/Search
Maps: from log in docs.Logs let trace = LoadDocument("traces/" + log.TraceId, "Traces") select new { Body = log.Body, ServiceName = log.ServiceName, Timestamp = (DateTime)log.Timestamp, SeverityText = log.SeverityText, SeverityNumber = log.SeverityNumber, ScopeName = log.ScopeName, TraceId = log.TraceId, TimestampMinute = new DateTime(((DateTime)log.Timestamp).Year, ((DateTime)log.Timestamp).Month, ((DateTime)log.Timestamp).Day, ((DateTime)log.Timestamp).Hour, ((DateTime)log.Timestamp).Minute, 0), SeverityScope = log.SeverityText + "|" + log.ScopeName, HasPayment = trace != null && trace.HasPayment == true, HasFrontend = trace != null && trace.HasFrontend == true, HasCart = trace != null && trace.HasCart == true }

Indexes.Name: Logs/Fuzzy
Maps: from log in docs.Logs select new { Body = log.Body, Timestamp = (DateTime)log.Timestamp, ServiceName = log.ServiceName, ScopeName = log.ScopeName }
